blocks.content:
• Earth is a GEOID.
• Seasons due to tilt mad revolution , NOT distance.
• Sidereal day is shorter.
• Coriolis zero at equator.
• Northern winter near perihelion.

items: Exams often trap students into thinking distance causes seasons; remember it is tilt and revolution.
Questions frequently test Coriolis force magnitude at the equator—it is always zero.
Counter-intuitively, Northern Hemisphere winter occurs when Earth is near perihelion (closest point to the Sun).

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The true physical shape of the Earth is defined as a GEOID, not a perfect sphere.
Seasons are driven by axial tilt and orbital revolution, not by varying distance from the Sun.
A sidereal day is shorter in duration compared to a standard solar day.
The Coriolis force is completely absent (zero) at the equator.
The Northern Hemisphere experiences winter when Earth is near perihelion (closest to the Sun).
